Instructions to Candidates
  • This university examination consists of two 60-minute sections totaling 36 questions (36 marks).
  • Part A (Questions 1–18) covers first-order separable/linear/exact ODEs, second-order linear homogeneous ODEs, Wronskian, undetermined coefficients, and variation of parameters.
  • Part B (Questions 19–36) covers Laplace transforms, Dirac delta/step forcing, linear systems & phase planes, power series/Frobenius, and RK4 numerical methods.

1 Systems of Linear ODEs Foundational [1 mark]
In this problem, the matrix of x′=Ax\mathbf x'=A\mathbf xx′=Ax has eigenvalues 2 and 1. The origin is a:
A. stable spiral
B. center (stable, not asymptotically)
C. stable node
D. unstable node
Correct Answer: (D) — unstable node
Real eigenvalues of opposite sign give a saddle; same sign gives a node (stable if negative). Here: unstable node.

5 Nonhomogeneous Equations, Undetermined Coefficients & Resonance Foundational [1 mark]
Consider the nonhomogeneous second-order linear differential equation y′′+4y=8y'' + 4y = 8y′′+4y=8. What is the particular solution, yp(x)y_p(x)yp​(x), to this equation?
A. 2sin⁡(2x)2\sin(2x)2sin(2x)
B. 2cos⁡(2x)2\cos(2x)2cos(2x)
C. 222
D. 2x2x2x
Correct Answer: (C) — 222
The given differential equation is y′′+4y=8y'' + 4y = 8y′′+4y=8. This is a nonhomogeneous second-order linear differential equation. We use the method of undetermined coefficients to find a particular solution, yp(x)y_p(x)yp​(x). The nonhomogeneous term is a constant, 8. We guess a particular solution of the form yp(x)=Ay_p(x) = Ayp​(x)=A, where A is a constant. Then, yp′(x)=0y_p'(x) = 0yp′​(x)=0 and yp′′(x)=0y_p''(x) = 0yp′′​(x)=0. Substituting these into the differential equation: 0+4(A)=80 + 4(A) = 80+4(A)=8. Solving for A, we get 4A=84A = 84A=8, which means A=2A = 2A=2. Therefore, the particular solution is yp(x)=2y_p(x) = 2yp​(x)=2.

B. 200 kg200\text{ kg}200 kg
C. 350 kg350\text{ kg}350 kg
D. 250 kg250\text{ kg}250 kg

Changing volume: V(t)=100+(4−2)t=100+2tV(t) = 100 + (4 - 2)t = 100 + 2tV(t)=100+(4−2)t=100+2t. Multiplying gives ((t+50)S)′=8(t+50)((t + 50)S)' = 8(t + 50)((t+50)S)′=8(t+50). Integrating gives (t+50)S=4(t+50)2+C(t + 50)S = 4(t + 50)^2 + C(t+50)S=4(t+50)2+C. Using S(0)=0S(0) = 0S(0)=0 yields 50(0)=4(2500)+C  ⟹  C=−1000050(0) = 4(2500) + C \implies C = -1000050(0)=4(2500)+C⟹C=−10000. Thus S(t)=4(t+50)−10000t+50S(t) = 4(t + 50) - \frac{10000}{t + 50}S(t)=4(t+50)−t+5010000​. At t=50t = 50t=50, S(50)=4(100)−10000100=400−100=300 kgS(50) = 4(100) - \frac{10000}{100} = 400 - 100 = 300\text{ kg}S(50)=4(100)−10010000​=400−100=300 kg.
